description:
Every `jmap-*-server` crate carries this pattern in its `[dev-dependencies]`:

```toml
[dev-dependencies]
jmap-mail-server = { workspace = true, features = ["memory", "mdn", "sieve"] }
```

The workspace dep expands to `{ path = "...", version = "0.1" }`. On `cargo publish`, cargo strips `path` and resolves the self-dev-dep against the registry. When the new features (`memory`, `mdn`, `sieve`) didn't exist in the previously-published versions of the crate, resolution fails with:

```
package `jmap-mail-server` depends on `jmap-mail-server` with feature `mdn` but `jmap-mail-server` does not have that feature.
failed to select a version for `jmap-mail-server` which could resolve this conflict
```

`--no-verify` doesn't help — the error fires during pre-publish manifest resolution, not during the build-verify step.

Affects all 8 server crates: mail-server, chat-server, contacts-server, calendars-server, tasks-server, filenode-server, sharing-server, metadata-server.

## Workaround used on 2026-05-13 publish

For the 0.1.x publish round on 2026-05-13, the dev-dep self-reference was temporarily commented out in each crate's Cargo.toml, the crate was published with `--allow-dirty`, then the comment-out was reverted. This works but is operationally ugly — every future publish needs the same dance.

## Permanent fix options

1. **Drop the dev-dep self-reference entirely.** Move tests that need the `memory` feature into a separate test-only crate in the workspace, or into the crate's own `tests/` directory with a `#[cfg(feature = "memory")]` gate that requires building with `cargo test --features memory`. This is the cleanest fix; cost is documenting how to run tests.

2. **`[target.'cfg(any())'.dev-dependencies]` trick.** Hides the dep from cargo's resolver entirely. But also hides it from `cargo test` of the source tree, so it doesn't actually let tests run with the features. Not a real fix.

3. **Two-step publish.** Publish a version with the dev-dep removed, then add it back and publish the next version. The next-next version can then resolve against the previous (which has the features). Two publishes per release — operationally worse than the workaround.

4. **Resolver=2 with manifest version pin.** Possibly cargo's v2 resolver handles this better with `version = "=X.Y.Z"` pinning. Untested.

Recommended path: option 1. The `memory` feature is intentionally opt-in for downstream callers, and the test entry point can be the same crate's `tests/` directory with `#![cfg(feature = "memory")]` at the top.

## Acceptance

- Publishing any `jmap-*-server` crate to a new version succeeds without temporary Cargo.toml edits
- `cargo test -p jmap-mail-server --features memory,mdn,sieve` still runs the integration tests
- Documentation in workspace AGENTS.md and RELEASING.md updated to describe the new test invocation

LABELS: publish-readiness, refactor, canonical-template-sweep
title: Server crate publish: self-dev-dep + feature pattern blocks new releases
